column1: # Secret patterns read by hooks/scan.sh. Data rows carry four TAB-separated fields:
#   kind  label  flags  pattern
# kind: secret (the whole match is the value), assigned (the value is what follows the first : or =,
#   past quotes and spaces) or placeholder (a value any placeholder row matches is released, not flagged).
# label: the deny message names it. flags: - (case-sensitive) or i (case-insensitive).
# pattern: the subset POSIX ERE (GNU grep -E) and JavaScript RegExp without the u or v flag read identically:
#   no [[:class:]], no lookaround, no backreferences, a backslash only before ] . [ + * ? ( ) { } | ^ $ / -
#   (never inside brackets), no space at either end (write an edge space as [ ]). No field may hold a tab.
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are skipped. Secret and assigned rows are tried in file order;
#   the first with a non-placeholder match names the deny. A value of one repeated character is also
#   a placeholder; that rule is code in scan.sh, not a row.
# scan.sh denies every write it scans when this file is missing, any line carries a carriage return,
#   a row is not four non-empty fields, a kind or flag is unknown, a pattern starts or ends with a space,
#   holds [[: [[. [[= a [:class:] (? or \1-\9, escapes a character outside the list above, does not
#   compile under grep -E or matches the empty string, a placeholder row matches the secret-shaped probe
#   in scan.sh, or no secret row exists.
#   Not checked: a backslash inside brackets, a collating element later in a bracket ([a[.x.]]), a
#   placeholder word a real secret can contain.
